synopsis: Structure from motion matches points across photographs taken from different positions and solves for camera positions and three-dimensional point locations [f13145, f13144]. In drone or ground photogrammetry, it works with multi-view stereo to turn overlapping, calibrated images into camera poses and sparse geometry, followed by dense point clouds, textured meshes and surfaces [f3794]. The same combination can reconstruct poses, dense points and a textured mesh from a camera-only log [f3988]. Reconstruction from a working machine's recordings can instead combine camera, lidar, IMU and GNSS logs through structure from motion, lidar-inertial SLAM, point-cloud fusion and surfel or mesh generation [f3806]. The glossary identifies COLMAP as a widely used free structure-from-motion program and distinguishes the method from scene reconstruction, the full process of producing a usable virtual site [f13144].

relations.note: Explains point matching and joint estimation behind the glossary's recovery definition.
